CREATE FUNCTION [dbo].[ufnGetStock](@ProductID [int])
RETURNS [int]
AS
-- Returns the stock level for the product. This function is used internally only
BEGIN
    DECLARE @ret int;
   
    SELECT @ret = SUM(p.[Quantity])
    FROM [Production].[ProductInventory] p
    WHERE p.[ProductID] = @ProductID
        AND p.[LocationID] = '6'; -- Only look at inventory in the misc storage
   
    IF (@ret IS NULL)
        SET @ret = 0
   
    RETURN @ret
END;

      FROM production.product_inventory AS p

$$;

notes: Step 4 finding: SQL Server 2025 inlines this scalar function into the calling query (sys.sql_modules.is_inlineable = 1, Froid). PostgreSQL runs the function once per call, so per-row calls cost about 2x more at 20,000 calls. Equivalence is unaffected; a caller that needs the speed would inline the expression or use a set-based join. A PL/pgSQL version (dbo.ufnGetStock, 2026-11-12) measured slower than the LANGUAGE sql one (160 ms vs 123 ms at 20,000 calls), so the SQL version is kept.

Step 4 factor: 2.5x, not the default 1.5x, agreed by Steve Harlow (project owner, ruling F1) on 2026-11-18 (verification-standard.md, "unless the object's record states a different agreed factor"). Reason: SQL Server 2025 inlines this scalar function into the calling query (Froid); PostgreSQL cannot inline a function that reads a table, and 20,000 calls that read no row at all already take 99-116 ms (measured 2026-11-18), at or above 1.5x before any lookup. An extra or covering index does not help (measured: 110 -> 101 ms, 144 -> 153 ms). Results are the same (step 3); a caller that needs the speed uses a set-based join (7 ms measured). Agreed after the 1.5x measurements, not before.

Verified in an isolated scratch database: the original T-SQL is deployed unchanged; tables contain only the columns the object references, with no foreign key constraints and no pre-existing rows. Every foreign-key column is indexed on both engines (a modelling assumption for the runtime step).
